rationales: Alkali metals have one valence electron, not two.
The outer electronic configuration of alkali metals is ns¹.
ns²np⁵ is the valence configuration of halogens.
ns¹np is not the general configuration of alkali metals.
Chalk solution is a suspension rather than the intended colloid example.
Paints are colloids and show the Tyndall effect.
Sugar solution is a true solution and does not show the Tyndall effect.
Jelly is a colloid and also shows the Tyndall effect, so this question has more than one correct option.
Changing external pressure changes the boiling point.
Intermolecular forces affect the boiling point.
The starting temperature affects how long boiling takes, not the boiling point at a given pressure.
The nature of a liquid affects its boiling point.
NaCl is soluble in water.
C₆H₆ is nonpolar and is not soluble in water.
MgCl₂ is soluble in water.
KBr is soluble in water.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it.
N₂ has a complete octet around each nitrogen atom.
O₂ has a complete octet around each oxygen atom in its Lewis structure.
NH₃ has a complete octet around nitrogen.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among these halogens.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is not 1.0.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is not 2.6.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is approximately 4.0.
Fluorine's Pauling electronegativity is not 3.0.
The K shell has one subshell.
The M shell has three subshells: 3s, 3p, and 3d.
The O shell has five subshells.
The L shell has two subshells.
One water molecule has a mass of approximately 18 atomic mass units.
18 g is the mass of one mole of water, not one molecule.
18 mg is not the mass of one water molecule.
18 kg is not the mass of one water molecule.
Eight electrons are not involved in a triple covalent bond.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons form two shared pairs, which make a double bond.
Three electrons cannot form three shared pairs.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is the heaviest option and diffuses slowest.
J.J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model, not the concept of atomic orbits.
Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom.
Bohr presented the concept of electrons occupying orbits around the nucleus.
Planck introduced the quantum hypothesis, not the concept of atomic orbits.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Butter is a gel-type colloid in which liquid is dispersed in a solid.
Bronze is a solid solution of solids, not a liquid in a solid.
Fog is liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the Periodic Table.
Groups are the vertical columns of the Periodic Table.
Rows is another term for horizontal periods.
Blocks classify elements by the subshell being filled, not by vertical columns.
The second and third periods are called short periods.
Normal periods is not the standard name for the second and third periods.
Long periods generally refer to the fourth and fifth periods.
Very long periods refer to the sixth and seventh periods.
